comment: Credit where it is due: putting the NCI registry at rank 2 serves prefers_trials now, while the patient is NED and there is nothing measurable to enroll on. But at recurrence you sequence the trial route below sunitinib and regorafenib, and a patient whose stated preference is trials wants that menu offered co-equal with sunitinib, not after two guideline TKIs. Worth saying too that prefers_trials was defaulted here, not elicited, so I would confirm it before it carries this much ordering weight.

Bundling the NCI registry into rank 1 is the right instinct, it honors prefers_trials while the patient is NED, and your call to run the SDHB re-cut now is exactly what keeps trial eligibility from lapsing. Where we part is the recurrence ladder: ranking sunitinib ahead of the trial agents optimizes for the toxicity you can predict, but the stated preference is trials, so the trial route belongs alongside sunitinib rather than behind it. With no toxicity vetoes on file, the predictability premium buys this patient less than it would a tox-averse one.

This is the pick that protects the patient's trial preference, and I want it on record as such. SDHB reading intact against biallelic SDHA would quietly disqualify this patient at screening for every dSDH contingency trial, so getting the re-cut done now is what keeps prefers_trials from becoming a dead letter at first recurrence. One tissue pull, no therapeutic toxicity, and it guards the eligibility the patient says they want.

Your hold on active therapy now is right for an NED patient and I am glad it is explicit, dosing FGFR or TKI toxicity into someone with no measurable target would be harm for nothing. But ranking rogaratinib first when its trial is closed to accrual and access means compassionate use under-serves a patient whose actual preference is trials; the recruiting in-subtype pemigatinib study at your rank 2 is the one that cashes prefers_trials. Lead with the door that opens.
